data.text:
Are Southeast Asian players really useless? (15)

 No. It is just a difference in how you frame it.

 X started showing user regions, and ever since then the timeline has been on fire.

 Ronin’s recent downward trend does not look like it came from 'low quality' Southeast Asian players at all.

 It looks much closer to a case where the incentive system, which is tuned around Southeast Asian users, just is not that compelling.

 Minimum wage in Korea is about $7 an hour. In Los Angeles is $17 an hour. In most of Southeast Asia it is several times lower than that.

 Because of that gap, when capital allocators open positions on the RON chain, the incentives they receive often feel disappointing. The math just does not clear the bar for them.

 That said, Axie did create a lot of wealthy people. A huge chunk of them are based in Southeast Asia.

Now look at the first month revenue data for Night Crows: 

▶️ Download ranking: Thailand > Philippines > Taiwan > Indonesia
▶️ Revenue ranking: Taiwan > United States > Thailand > Philippines

 The data does show that East Asian and Western users have higher value per head than Southeast Asian users. That part is real.

 But why do they spend so much money? Because they keep winning easily against the users you like to call useless.

 Even so, I do not buy the idea that Southeast Asian users are just there to leech off the game and shorten its lifespan. 

 First rule is this: can you generate profit on paper even if your users are only from Southeast Asia or Nigeria

 Second rule is this: are you actually willing to share that profit with the capital that comes in

 Third rule is this: to recognize that capital prefers exposed positions, not piles of trapped value sitting inside the game economy.

 If your goal is to keep recycling all that revenue back into chain players and only chain players, you are not going to relive the PIXELS era forever.

 Back then my friends and I were literally playing the game for the PIXELS token.

Creating a QT thread here to add some nuance to this (read Gabby’s tweet and read the first comment from @apixtwts)

It’s incredibly valuable for game teams to have a presence at @YGGPlaySummit because they are some of the only people to actually crack the code of “web3 gaming”

Apix says that the SEA region brings players that are low value and extractive, and I think that is becoming an EXTREMELY lazy take

For this industry to work, we can’t blanket ignore regions because they want “smth-to-earn”

We HAVE to start designing systems that align different cohorts in gaming

This thesis we have had for years will simply not work if we only target T1 regions hoping to find whales. We will continue to did a slow death if that is the case.

From a game and economy design standpoint, we need to be better. We need to find a way to get the “x-to-earn” and the whale cohorts aligned within the game structure so that both groups are having meaningful game experiences. 

This isn’t novel, it’s common in every successful P2W game. Whales pay for an advantage, but they need to feel rewarded for spend. That typically comes from beating up on players who don’t spend. In the games industry the term is literally “cannon fodder”. 

We aren’t going to learn how to align these cohorts without better understanding of what people actually want. 

YGGPS is the top gaming event we have as an industry. 

If you’re building a web3 game, you need to understand where web3 games are clicking and where they are breaking. 

Go to the summit.
